comparison: Both evaluate EPCAM+ cell characterization (C6, C7, C56). OpenEval finds the data SUPPORTED with clear characterization, while peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY about the heterogeneous population, specifically questioning what the 45% of EPCAM+ cells with low PDX1/NKX6-1 represent and requesting integration with prior work.

Both address GP2+ population multipotency (C1, C9, C10, C57). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED but acknowledges C72's uncertainty about true multipotency. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAIN evaluation, questioning the multipotency interpretation and requesting additional marker analysis (PTF1a, Cpa1, c-Myc). Both accept descriptive data but differ on functional interpretation confidence.

Both evaluate temporal sequence of endocrine differentiation (C3, C13, C14, C58). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with well-documented temporal progression. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, accepting the sequential marker expression without concerns. Strong agreement on this developmental sequence.

Both address population structure and marker enrichment (C8, C12, C70, with peer also including C11, C69). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with multi-modal validation. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, accepting population definitions and comparative analysis, requesting only additional validation with independent datasets but not challenging core findings.

Both evaluate detailed subpopulation characterization using CD142 and SUSD2 (C20-C25, C61, C67, C68, C71). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with robust single-cell data. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, accepting the refinement of characterization and heterogeneity data without challenge. Strong agreement on this detailed analysis.

Both address bifurcation model and temporal insulin expression (C26, C62). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on temporal patterns and lineage marker enrichment, noting lack of direct lineage tracing. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, with surprise at the temporal pattern and questions about whether distinct β-cell populations exist. Divergence on interpretation confidence.

Both evaluate hPSC-fetal pancreas comparison (C5, C64-C66). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as critical validation. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, requesting clarification on which hPSC lines were used and noting decreased novelty due to recent prior publication. Agreement on basic comparison but concerns about methodological details.

Both address methodological and ethical compliance (C63-C66). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with clear description. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, questioning precision of developmental timing, whether replicates are biological or technical, and requesting full details in supplementary table. Divergence on adequacy of methodological reporting.

Both address background knowledge and prior work (C27-C54, C55, C77-C78). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, accepting these as established facts providing scientific foundation. Complete agreement on contextual claims.

Both address explicit limitations and uncertainties (C72-C76). OpenEval categorizes as UNCERTAIN, noting honest assessment of what cannot be concluded. Peer reviewers also categorize as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging these as speculative statements requiring additional data. Complete agreement that these represent unresolved questions.

OpenEval evaluates GP2hi enrichment in acinar markers (C2, C11, C69) as SUPPORTED with convergent evidence from multiple approaches. No corresponding isolated peer review evaluation found, though C2 and C11 appear in peer R1 and R4 respectively within broader contexts.

OpenEval evaluates temporal marker expression changes (C4, C15-C19, C59) as SUPPORTED with statistical significance across developmental stages. Peer reviewers address subsets of these claims in R2 and R5 but no single peer result corresponds to this complete temporal progression evaluation.

OpenEval evaluates fetal characteristics in hPSC-derived cells (C55) as SUPPORTED, providing context for studying human fetal development. While C55 appears in peer R9's claim list, it is grouped with extensive background claims rather than evaluated separately.
